{{Short description|Principle of circuitry}}
In a [[digital circuit]] or system, '''static discipline''' is a guarantee on logical elements that "if inputs meet valid input thresholds, then the system guarantees outputs will meet valid output thresholds", named by Stephen A. Ward and Robert H. Halstead in 1990, but practiced for decades earlier.<ref>{{cite book|title=The Integrated Circuit Data Book|date=1968|publisher=Motorola Semiconductor Products, Inc.|pages=2.81–2.84|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2V42AQAAIAAJ&q=voh+vol+vih+vil+circuits}}</ref>

The valid output thresholds voltages ''V''<sub>OH</sub> (output high) and ''V''<sub>OL</sub> (output low), and valid input thresholds ''V''<sub>IH</sub> (input high) and ''V''<sub>IL</sub> (input low), satisfy a [[robustness principle]] such that

:''V''<sub>OL</sub> < ''V''<sub>IL</sub> < ''V''<sub>IH</sub> <  ''V''<sub>OH</sub>

with sufficient [[noise margin]]s in the inequalities.<ref>{{cite book|author=Stephen A. Ward and Robert H. Halstead|title=Computation Structures|date=1990|publisher=MIT Press|isbn=9780262231398|pages=5–7|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=m1973nU88yoC&pg=PA5}}</ref>
